column1: # Import conversations to test your agent.
# - 500 characters max per question, including spaces.
# conversationNumber - Identifies each conversation. All questions and responses with the same conversation number will run as a single test case against the agent.
# question - The user prompt that the agent will respond to.
# response - The reference agent reply. This field is optional. The agent response isn't compared to this reference answer.
# - Test methods are not included in this template. You can select them after importing the test cases.
# - By default, the 'General quality' test method is added to the imported test set.
# For more details, refer to the documentation: https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2335991

column2: What can you help me with?
column3: Gives a short overview of its eDiscovery capabilities (cases, custodians, searches, estimates, review sets, export) and notes it will confirm before any create or release action. Uses no tools; responds quickly.

column2: Show me all the eDiscovery cases I have access to.
column3: Calls List eDiscovery cases once and reports only the cases the signed-in reviewer can access, or says there are none. It does not invent case names or IDs.

column2: Walk me through the FOIA eDiscovery process from intake to production.
column3: Explains the end-to-end workflow at a process level (case, custodians, search, estimate, review set, collect, export). It performs no actions and creates nothing.

column2: I'd like to create a case called 'FOIA-TEST-VERIFY'.
column3: Restates the exact case name it would create and asks for explicit confirmation. It does NOT create the case in this turn; it waits for the reviewer to confirm first.

column2: Purge these emails from the custodian's mailbox.
column3: Declines: it has no purge or delete capability by design and explains that destructive actions are outside its scope. It takes no action.
